clue.text: Create pollution in a gorge

definitions.meaning: to make something dirty or impure, as a verb
a narrow pass or valley that troops must march through in single file

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make foul or impure; the noun is a narrow ravine or pass, two unrelated senses of one spelling.

clue.text: Notes having exposed members

definitions.meaning: the word is spelt entirely from musical notes
with trousers pulled off as a prank, leaving the legs bare

explanation.definitionFit: Debagged is British slang for having had one's trousers removed, and its letters are all names of musical notes.

clue.text: Side-effects of quarrel, in a word

definitions.meaning: unwanted consequences of an event
the two-word phrasal verb meaning to quarrel, run together as a single word

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means adverse after-effects, and written as two words it is the verb for having a quarrel.

clue.text: US S airman repositioned behind girl, one I abandoned

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are put into new positions
a letter is left out of those being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one of the two letters I in the fodder

explanation.surface: A girl's position shifts as an American pilot moves in behind her, someone having walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: BEHIND GIRL has ten letters; 'abandoned' drops one I and 'repositioned' rearranges the other nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh was the American aviator who made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 1927.

clue.text: Henry combined with the author to better advantage — or the opposite

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
and means together with
the setter referring to themself gives I
to cap something is to outdo or better it

explanation.surface: A man called Henry teams up with the writer to gain an edge, or perhaps lose one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works both ways: in racing a handicap is the weight given to level the field, a burden to one and an advantage to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a disadvantage imposed, or the start given to weaker competitors, so it covers both an edge and its reverse.

clue.text: Where goods may be displayed, in disarray

definitions.meaning: read literally, throughout a retail store
an informal British idiom for scattered everywhere and disorganised

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means chaotic or scattered everywhere, and read literally it describes merchandise spread across a store.

clue.text: The oldest of the members in party have desires

parts.note: a do is an informal party
to yen is to yearn or long for something

explanation.surface: The senior member of the club wants something at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the senior or most respected member of a group.

clue.text: Small volume about drink, work of the highest quality

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: cc is cubic centimetres, a small measure of volume
lassi is a yoghurt drink from India

explanation.surface: A slim book about drinking turns out to be a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small volume' looks like a slim book; it is cc, cubic centimetres, which 'about' places round LASSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work acknowledged as being of lasting excellence.

clue.text: About to be shot, perhaps? That's puzzling

definitions.meaning: holding still for a photographer who is about to take a picture
presenting a difficulty, as when a question poses a problem

explanation.definitionFit: Someone modelling for a camera is in position to be photographed, and a question that is puzzling is posing a problem.

clue.text: Book the former students preserve is tragic novel

parts.note: Jude is a book of the New Testament
taken as written
OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A book about keeping former students alive turns out to be a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: OB is the British abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's last novel is notoriously bleak, ending with the deaths of the hero's children and of Jude himself.

clue.text: Speaking in tongues? Minimally so

parts.note: the religious phrase is read literally: someone who speaks in languages, and at the least two of them

explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in two languages speaks in more than one tongue, which is the smallest number that makes the plural true.

clue.text: Poet mostly indistinguishable from Keats? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.text: Poet mostly indistinguishable from Keats? Doesn't sound like it

parts.words: Poet mostly indistinguishable from Keats? Doesn't sound like it
parts.note: an Irish poet whose surname on paper differs from the Romantic poet's by one letter, yet is pronounced to rhyme with 'gates', not 'beats'

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish poet's surname is written like the English Romantic's with only the first letter changed, though it is said quite differently.

clue.text: From what we hear, bargain so long

indicators.note: signals that the word is chosen for how it is said aloud, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that a cheap deal has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell, a parting phrase with the same meaning.

clue.text: Meat is in new oven, cooked

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the other letters
cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook reports that the meat is roasting in a brand-new oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' reads as the meat's state, but it signals the anagram of N plus oven, giving VENON, and 'in' sets the clue's own little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Penetrate the heart of America, without leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped, leader being the front

parts.note: the American spelling of the word for the middle point

explanation.surface: An explorer pushes into the American interior with nobody in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The US spelling CENTER, losing its first letter C to 'without leader', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to go into it, so penetrate is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Work that's bound to be inflexible

definitions.text: Work that's bound to be inflexible

parts.words: Work that's bound to be inflexible
parts.note: a book whose binding is in stiff boards, so it cannot bend like a paperback

explanation.definitionFit: A book bound in stiff covers is a stiff-backed work, by definition rigid rather than flexible.

clue.text: Gambler, before start of race, having lost less

parts.note: a better is one who places bets
the off is the start of a horse race

explanation.surface: A punter, just before the horses set off, finds he has lost less than feared.
explanation.definitionFit: To be better off is to be in a more favourable position, here one with smaller losses.

clue.text: Cow not straying into marshland

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the Fens of eastern England
right means correct, not deviating from the true path

explanation.surface: A cow that does not wander ends up in the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a verb here, to intimidate, not the farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, the same as scaring them into submission.

clue.text: Bears ridicule

definitions.meaning: the honey-loving bear of the A. A. Milne stories, named twice for two of him
to dismiss scornfully as nonsense, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Two of Milne's teddy bear side by side make a reduplicated word meaning to scoff at or dismiss something.

clue.text: Fleet, for example, taking alternative to deep blue sea

definitions.meaning: the Fleet was a historic London prison, so a former jail, nick being slang for prison
the idiom 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' sets the devil against the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a nickname for Satan, the devil of the idiom, and read literally means a former jail like the Fleet.

clue.text: Mount was beaten with stick

definitions.meaning: the mountain in Galilee traditionally linked to the Transfiguration
a small drum of old, played with a single stick

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a biblical mountain in Israel and a small medieval drum that a player struck with a stick.

clue.text: Like each part of 18, anticipating fall in prices

definitions.meaning: each half of the answer at 18 is the name of a teddy bear, so it is bear-like
stock-market term for expecting prices to drop

explanation.definitionFit: A bear in markets expects prices to fall, and the word also simply means resembling a bear.

clue.text: Male head set up term of French, it's appropriate to say

definitions.text: term of French, it's appropriate to say

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A man raises his head to say something apt in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the whole run TOMNOB, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon mot is a French phrase for a witty or well-chosen remark, literally a good word.

clue.text: Solver of riddle I posed and you pronounced silly

indicators.note: silly suggests these letters are put into a foolish new order

parts.note: taken as written
the letter U is said exactly like the word you

explanation.surface: A man boasts that he and you, looking foolish, struck a pose to puzzle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sphinx asked who walks on four legs, then two, then three; this Theban hero answered man and freed the city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this king of Thebes solved the riddle of the Sphinx.

clue.text: Bothering person over nothing — what sauce!

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An annoying person fusses over nothing, and what cheek it is!
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts PEST above O. 'sauce' looks like cheek in the exclamation but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Matter revealed in report on novel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
a report is a loud bang, as from a gun

explanation.surface: A news item about a book reveals what it is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the idiom 'the whole shebang', meaning the whole matter or affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is slang for an affair or business, as in the whole thing or matter.

clue.text: They're located in cockpit as source of power

definitions.meaning: matches between fighting cocks, staged in the pit, are called by an old word for a contest
the supply of electricity, gas or water from a central network

explanation.definitionFit: The word means cockfights held in a cockpit, and also the public supply lines that bring electricity to a building.

clue.text: He lacks certain knowledge about the craft he studies

definitions.text: He lacks certain knowledge about the craft he studies

parts.words: He lacks certain knowledge about the craft he studies
parts.note: the craft are flying saucers whose nature is by definition unidentified, so their student cannot know for sure what they are

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies unidentified flying objects researches craft that, by their name, nobody has identified.

clue.text: Business deal as reason for director to demand cut?

definitions.meaning: the acquisition of one company by another

definitions.text: reason for director to demand cut?
definitions.meaning: a film director shouts cut and asks for the scene to be shot again when a take goes wrong

explanation.definitionFit: It is a corporate acquisition, and read as two words it is a filmed shot that must be redone after the director calls a halt.

clue.text: Type of hound giving tongue

definitions.meaning: a long-haired breed of hunting dog
a language, here Pashto, the language of Afghanistan

explanation.definitionFit: It names a long-haired breed of hunting dog and also Pashto, a language spoken in Afghanistan.
